notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 132 because the research step failed before I could read a single page.

I tried to open six sources: Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org, and the NET Bible notes. The system stopped the request and said I had no more tool calls left for this turn, so nothing loaded. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't drafted anything rather than guess.

If you send the request again in a new turn, I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-132/
  - biblehub.com commentaries on Psalm 132 by Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Barnes
  - Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (on spurgeon.org or studylight.org)
  - preceptaustin.org
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:**
  - Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu)
  - Lutheran material (lcms.org, 1517.org)
  - Reformed and Baptist teachers (ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org)
  - Pentecostal sources (ag.org, samstorms.org)
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org translator's notes and bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship
  - Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org, where this psalm is numbered 131 (the older Greek and Latin Bibles number most psalms one lower)
  - catholic.com and oca.org for Catholic and Orthodox readings

Then I'll write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point and leave out anything I can't find.
